# Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (v2026.8.13)

**Release Date:** August 13, 2026

> Patch release. This tag rolls up the ~656 PRs merged since v0.20.0 into a stable tagged release for downstream consumers (Docker images, hosted deployments, and anyone installing from the latest tag).

---

## About this release

Since v0.20.0 (August 3), this window landed **1,444 commits** across **~656 merged PRs**, touching **2,172 files** (+233,872 / −75,244), and closed **~481 issues**. It is a broad stabilization-and-fixes rollup spanning the desktop app, gateway platforms, installers, tool system, and provider catalogs.

**Full curated release notes for this window will ship with v0.21.0**, which will document everything from v0.20.0 onward — highlights, feature areas, and complete contributor credits. Nothing in this window is skipped.

## Updating

- Existing installs: `hermes update`
- Fresh install: see the installer one-liner in the [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent#readme)

**Full Changelog**: [v2026.8.3...v2026.8.13](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/compare/v2026.8.3...v2026.8.13)

signals.title: [Bug]: Hermes Desktop spawns unbounded serve processes on reconnection — old processes not cleaned up
signals.text: ### Bug Description hermes_cli.main serve has no --replace flag (unlike gateway run --replace) Desktop's reconnection logic spawns a new serve but doesn't SIGTERM the prior one With sustained model API errors (403/network issues), processes accumulate at ~1 per 15-30 min Suggest: add --replace semantics to serve, or have desktop kill old PID before spawning new one ### Steps to Reproduce Diagnosis Symptom: 26 Hermes serve processes currently running, all alive (no zombies). Timeline: 00:18 — First serve launched (default profile) 00:47 onwards — ams3 serve processes spawned every 15-30 minutes, continuing until 08:59 Each uses --port 0 (random port), so they don't conflict with each other Root Cause: Hermes Desktop GUI's serve reconnection logic has a bug ~/.hermes/logs/desktop.log shows cascading retries: 代码 ⏳ Retrying in 2.7s (attempt 1/4)... ⏳ Retrying in 5.5s (attempt 2/4)... ⏳ Retrying in 10.2s (attempt 3/4)... ⚠️ custom stream drop (RemoteProtocolError) after 133.7s — reconnecting Along with model API errors (HTTP 403 from expired/revoked API keys). On each reconnect, the desktop spawns a new serve child process but never kills the old one. Comparison: The gateway command has a --replace flag, so launchd properly replaces the old process on restart. The serve command has no --replace logic, so old processes accumulate indefinitely. Full chain: Serve processes remain alive (listening on random ports) Desktop calls model API through serve → API returns HTTP 403 (expired/revoked key) Desktop misinterprets this as a serve connection failure → triggers reconnection Reconnection logic spawns a new serve (hermes_cli.main serve --host ... --port 0) Does not kill the old one → old process leaks Continuous retries → continuous accumulation 26 processes by morning. Suggested fix for the issue: Add --replace semantics to the serve subcommand (similar to gateway run --replace), OR Have the desktop kill the old PID before spawning a new serve process ### Expected Behavior 预期行为：当桌面应用程序重新连接或重新启动服务后端时，应该在生成新进程之前优雅地终止之前的服务进程（通过SIGTERM）。或者，serve子命令应该支持——replace标志（类似于gateway run——replace），该标志可以在启动新进程之前自动停止绑定到相同配置文件的任何现有服务进程。这两种方法都可以防止孤立过程的积累。 ### Actual Behavior After a sustained period of model API errors (HTTP 403 from expired/revoked API keys), the Hermes Desktop GUI entered a reconnection loop. Each retry cycle spawned a new serve child process (python -m hermes_cli.main --profile ams3 serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0) but never terminated the previous one. Since serve uses --port 0 (random port), the new process never fails from port conflicts, so all old processes remain alive indefinitely. This resulted in 26 orphaned serve processes accumulated over ~8 hours (00:47 – 08:59), all listening on random ports and consuming system resources. The gateway run subcommand handles this correctly with its --replace flag, but serve has no equivalent mechanism. Desktop log showing the retry cascade: 代码 ⏳ Retrying in 2.7s (attempt 1/4)... ⏳ Retrying in 5.5s (attempt 2/4)... ⏳ Retrying in 10.2s (attempt 3/4)... ⚠️ custom stream drop (RemoteProtocolError) after 133.7s — reconnecting ❌ Non-retryable error (HTTP 403): HTTP 403: This API key has been revoked. GUI log confirming each spawn: 00:47:03 — Desktop cron scheduler started 00:47:04 — Desktop cron scheduler started 01:09:19 — Desktop cron scheduler started 01:09:20 — Desktop cron scheduler started ... (26 entries total, one pair per 15-30 min) Process tree confirmed all 26 were alive (non-zero CPU, non-zombie), each with a distinct PID and start time matching the GUI log timestamps. ### Affected Component Other ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) _No response_ ### Debug Report ```shell Non ``` ### Operating System macos 26.5.2 (25F84) ### Python Version python3.11 ### Hermes Version # v0.18.0 7e8f50a ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ```shell ``` ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) _No response_ ### Proposed Fix (optional) _No response_ ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

signals.title: [Feature]: Pluggable database backend for security-critical deployments
signals.text: ### Problem or Use Case Hermes Agent stores all data in hardcoded SQLite files. This is a fundamental security limitation that cannot be worked around at the application level. For a personal AI system that accumulates years of private conversations, sensitive knowledge, health information, political views, financial discussions, and everything else a person talks to their AI about - plaintext files on disk are problematic and unmanageable. ### Proposed Solution **What a pluggable backend solves** - **Encryption at rest:** Column-level or tablespace encryption via pgcrypto, TDE, or native database encryption - **Data compartmentalization:** Under compelled access, database credentials can be separate from system access - **Separate authentication:** Database credentials independent of filesystem access - **Row-level security:** PostgreSQL RLS for fine-grained access control over different data categories - **Centralized security management:** Same security policies, same backup/encryption strategy, same audit trail as the rest of the AI ecosystem ### Alternatives Considered _No response_ ### Feature Type Configuration option ### Scope Small (single file, < 50 lines) ### Contribution - [ ] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR ### Debug Report (optional) ```shell ```

signals.title: [Bug]:cua-driver macOS: ScreenCaptureKit display_count=0 despite TCC permissions OK (macOS 26.5.2 arm64)
signals.text: ### Bug Description ### Hermes version: v0.18.2 | cua-driver: 0.8.3 ### OS: macOS 26.5.2 (arm64) — Mac mini Apple Silicon #### Description Computer Use capture (`action='capture'`) returns width: 0, height: 0, 0 elements in any mode (`vision` ou `som`) and any app target (`Chrome`, `Safari`, `Discord`, ou sans app). #### `hermes computer-use doctor` output cua-driver 0.8.3 on darwin — ok platform_supported: macOS 26.5.2 (arm64) session_active: MCP session is active. tcc_accessibility: Accessibility is granted. tcc_screen_recording: Screen Recording is granted. ax_capability: AX is trusted and reachable. ⚠ screen_capture_capability: ScreenCaptureKit reachable; 0 display(s) shareable. Permissions TCC toutes OK, ScreenCaptureKit joignable, mais `display_count=0`. #### Ce qui marche - `action='list_apps'` ✅ liste correctement les applications en cours #### Ce qui ne marche pas - Toute `action='capture'` → sortie 0×0, aucun élément - Problème persistant après redémarrage du daemon et après upgrade cua-driver 0.6.8 → 0.8.3 - Se produit sur macOS 26.5.2 arm64 (Mac mini Apple Silicon) #### Feature request Ajouter un tool `vision_analyze(image_url)` pour que l'agent puisse soumettre des images directement à un modèle capable de vision (Grok 4.3, etc.) — cela permettrait de contourner ScreenCaptureKit quand il échoue. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Lancer `hermes computer-use doctor` → confirmer que toutes les permissions sont vertes mais que `display_count=0` 2. Exécuter `computer_use(action='capture', mode='vision', app='Google Chrome')` → retourne `width: 0, height: 0`, 0 éléments 3. Même résultat avec `mode='som'`, avec d'autres apps (`Safari`, `Discord`), ou sans paramètre `app` 4. Redémarrer le daemon cua-driver → toujours `display_count=0` 5. Upgrader cua-driver de 0.6.8 à 0.8.3 (via `hermes update`) → toujours `display_count=0` ### Expected Behavior computer_use(action='capture', mode='vision', app='Google Chrome')` devrait retourner une capture d'écran (image + dimensions réelles) de la fenêtre Chrome avec les éléments interactifs détectés. Le comportement attendu est un screenshot fonctionnel de l'application ciblée, comme décrit dans la documentation de Hermes Agent Computer Use. ### Actual Behavior `computer_use(action='capture', mode='vision', app='Google Chrome')` retourne `{"width": 0, "height": 0, "elements": [], "total_elements": 0}`. Aucune capture d'écran n'est produite, aucune fenêtre ni élément n'est détecté. Le daemon répond sans erreur mais ne voit aucun écran disponible (`display_count=0` dans ScreenCaptureKit). ### Affected Component Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.) ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) Discord ### Debug Report ```shell Debug report: https://paste.rs/BmjWe agent.log: https://paste.rs/RUIBG gateway.log: https://paste.rs/WDmJ9 gui.log: https://paste.rs/97pRe desktop.log: https://dpaste.com/4TYNQVNPM ``` ### Operating System macOS 26.5.2 (arm64) — Mac mini Apple Silicon ### Python Version Python 3.9.6 ### Hermes Version v0.18.2 (cua-driver 0.8.3) ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ```shell ``` ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) _No response_ ### Proposed Fix (optional) _No response_ ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

signals.title: bug(desktop): auto-generated hermes.desktop uses wrong Exec path, breaking KDE taskbar pinning
signals.text: bug(desktop): auto-generated hermes.desktop uses wrong Exec path, breaking KDE taskbar pinning ## Bug Description `hermes desktop` auto-registers a Linux `.desktop` entry every launch (introduced in eea6044, 2026-08-01). The `Exec` path is resolved via `sys.argv[0]`, which can point to a bare Python script instead of the venv wrapper — causing the launcher to silently fail when launched from KDE's application menu (cold start, no `PYTHONPATH`). Additionally, the auto-generated `.desktop` is **rewritten on every `hermes desktop` launch**, which causes KDE Plasma's taskbar to lose track of the pinned icon — clicking the pinned icon opens a new window instead of focusing the existing one. ## Environment - OS: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (Wayland session, KDE Plasma) - GPU: NVIDIA RTX 3080 (driver 595.84) - Hermes: v0.20.0 (git-installed, commit 863e313) - Electron: 40.10.2 ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Install Hermes via git, build desktop app 2. Run `hermes desktop` from terminal (using `~/.local/bin/hermes` wrapper) 3. Observe: `~/.local/share/applications/hermes.desktop` is auto-created with correct Exec path 4. Launch Hermes Desktop from KDE application menu → the `.desktop` is rewritten with `Exec=/home/.../hermes-agent/hermes desktop` (bare Python script) 5. Subsequent KDE menu launches fail silently (no `hermes_cli` on `sys.path`) 6. Pin the app to KDE taskbar → clicking the pinned icon after a relaunch opens a new instance instead of focusing the existing window ## Root Cause Two issues in `hermes_cli/linux_desktop_entry.py`: ### 1. `resolve_exec_command()` depends on `sys.argv[0]` *Due to network issues, it is not convenient to upload as an attachment* ```python # hermes_cli/relaunch.py — resolve_hermes_bin() def resolve_hermes_bin(): argv0 = sys.argv[0] # ← Whatever launched this process if os.path.isabs(argv0) and os.path.isfile(argv0) and os.access(argv0, os.X_OK): return argv0 ``` When launched from the wrapper (`~/.local/bin/hermes`) → Exec is correct. When launched from a bare script (`~/.hermes/hermes-agent/hermes`) → Exec is wrong. Once the `.desktop` flips to the bare-script path, it stays broken (self-reinforcing cycle). ### 2. `render_desktop_entry()` omits critical environment The generated `.desktop` has no `ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT=x11`, which is required on NVIDIA + Wayland systems (GPU process crashes otherwise). It also lacks `--skip-build`, causing unnecessary rebuilds on every menu launch. ## Expected Behavior 1. `Exec` should use a stable, environment-independent path (prefer `shutil.which("hermes")` or the known venv wrapper path, not `sys.argv[0]`) 2. The `.desktop` should NOT be rewritten if a user-customized version already exists 3. Consider adding `--skip-build` to the generated `Exec` line (rebuilding on every menu launch is wasteful) 4. Consider detecting NVIDIA + Wayland and adding `ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT=x11` automatically ## Workaround Users can manually maintain a separate `.desktop` file: ```desktop [Desktop Entry] Name=Hermes Desktop Exec=env ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT=x11 /home/$USER/.local/bin/hermes desktop --skip-build Icon=/home/$USER/.hermes/hermes-agent/apps/desktop/assets/icon.png Terminal=false Type=Application Categories=Development;System;Utility; StartupWMClass=Hermes ``` Then delete the auto-generated `hermes.desktop` after each launch.
signals.author: JDK-SHINANO

signals.title: [Bug]: computer_use silently discards app= and fails every app-scoped capture when a model emits placeholder pid=0 / window_id=0
signals.text: # [Bug]: `computer_use` silently discards `app=` and fails every app-scoped capture when a model emits placeholder `pid=0` / `window_id=0` ## Summary `_dispatch()` treats **any non-`None`** `pid`/`window_id` as a request for exact-window targeting. Several providers emit *every* declared schema property on *every* tool call, filling unused optional integers with `0`. For those models `pid=0, window_id=0` is present on all calls, so: 1. the exact-target branch is entered, 2. the caller's `app=` is **dropped on the floor**, 3. `_positive_int(0)` returns `None`, 4. the capture fails with `<capture targeting requires positive integer pid and window_id>`. Net effect: **`capture(app=...)` and frontmost capture never work at all** for that class of model — `computer_use` is unusable end-to-end, and the error message points the model at `pid`/`window_id`, which is the opposite of the real problem. Still present on `main` @ `b3aa561` (checked 2026-08-07). ## Environment | | | |---|---| | hermes-agent | `0.20.0`, bug verified on `origin/main` `b3aa561` | | OS | macOS 26.6 (25G72), Apple silicon | | cua-driver | 0.19.1 (daemon healthy, AX + Screen Recording granted) | | Python | 3.11.15 | | Triggering model | `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` via OpenRouter | | Non-triggering model | `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` via OpenRouter | ## Reproduction Any model that emits the full property set works. The payload below is copied verbatim from a real session (abridged — the ~40 remaining schema properties are likewise present and zero/empty-filled): ```json {"action":"capture","mode":"som","app":"Comet","pid":0,"window_id":0, "max_elements":100,"element":0,"coordinate":[0,0],"button":"left","modifiers":[], "seconds":0,"raise_window":false,"capture_after":false, ...} ``` **Expected:** capture the on-screen window belonging to `Comet`. **Actual:** ```json {"mode":"som","width":0,"height":0,"app":"", "window_title":"<capture targeting requires positive integer pid and window_id>", "elements":[],"total_elements":0} ``` Reproduced identically with `app="Comet"`, `app="/Applications/Comet.app"`, `app="ai.perplexity.comet"`, and with no `app` at all (frontmost capture). ## Root cause `tools/computer_use/tool.py:598` (`main` @ `b3aa561`): ```python capture_kwargs: Dict[str, Any] = {"mode": mode, "app": args.get("app")} if args.get("pid") is not None or args.get("window_id") is not None: # <-- 0 is not None capture_kwargs.update({ "pid": args.get("pid"), "window_id": args.get("window_id"), }) ``` `0` passes `is not None`, so the exact-target path is taken and `app` is discarded. `cua_backend.capture()` then rejects it via `_positive_int()` (`cua_backend.py:2247-2252`), which is correct behaviour for a genuine exact target — the defect is upstream of it, in how "was an exact target requested?" is decided. `0` is never a valid pid and never a valid window id, so it can be read as "not supplied" with no loss of expressiveness. ## Why this has gone unreported It is provider-dependent. Measured tool-call payloads from one machine: | Model | Properties emitted per call | `pid` / `window_id` when unused | |---|---|---| | `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` (OpenRouter) | ~45 — the entire schema | `0` / `0` → **bug fires** | | `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` (OpenRouter) | 1–4 | omitted → unaffected | Models that emit only the fields they mean never hit it, which is why a defect that makes the toolset totally non-functional can sit in `main` unnoticed. ## Proposed fix Read the two arguments through a helper that treats non-positive values as absent. Deliberately **keeps** the existing "both required" error when exactly one *real* id is supplied, so a half-specified exact target still fails loudly instead of silently falling back to app/frontmost discovery and misrouting input. ```diff +def _exact_target_arg(value: Any) -> Optional[int]: + """Read a pid/window_id capture argument, treating placeholders as absent. + + Several providers emit every declared property on every tool call and fill + the unused optional integers with 0. `0` is not a pid and not a window_id — + it means "no exact window was targeted". + """ + if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, str)): + return None + try: + parsed = int(value) + except ValueError: + return None + return parsed if parsed > 0 else None + + def _dispatch(backend: ComputerUseBackend, action: str, args: Dict[str, Any]) -> Any: ... capture_kwargs: Dict[str, Any] = {"mode": mode, "app": args.get("app")} - if args.get("pid") is not None or args.get("window_id") is not None: + target_pid = _exact_target_arg(args.get("pid")) + target_window_id = _exact_target_arg(args.get("window_id")) + if target_pid is not None or target_window_id is not None: capture_kwargs.update({ - "pid": args.get("pid"), - "window_id": args.get("window_id"), + "pid": target_pid, + "window_id": target_window_id, }) ``` Verified against the real failing payloads: | Call | Before | After | |---|---|---| | `capture(app="Comet", pid=0, window_id=0)` | `0×0`, 0 elements | `1456×834`, full AX tree | | `capture(app="", pid=0, window_id=0)` | `0×0`, 0 elements | `1455×837` frontmost | | `capture(pid=43217, window_id=100005)` | works | works (unchanged) | | `capture(app="X", pid=43217, window_id=0)` | wrong message | `requires both pid and window_id` (accurate) | ## Please also check #73252 [#73252](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/73252) extends exact `pid`+`window_id` targeting to the input actions (`click`, `drag`, `scroll`, `type`, `key`) using the same "both positive integers" contract. If it lands with the same `is not None` gating, this bug is propagated from `capture` to every input action for the same models. Worth applying the same helper there before merge. ## Secondary (happy to split into its own issue) When `app=` matches nothing, the failure message lists only naming causes: ``` <no on-screen window matched app='Comet'; call list_apps to see available app names or bundle IDs ...> ``` `_load_windows()` queries the driver with `on_screen_only`, so an app that is minimized or on another macOS Space is invisible to matching and the message gives the model no way forward. In practice the model then invents a `window_id` — in the session that produced this report it tried `window_id=1` and got `window_id 1 is not a live window`, which sent the whole debugging session down the wrong path. Note that `focus_app(..., raise_window=True)` is **not** a usable remedy here: `focus_app` resolves against the same on-screen-only list and returns `No on-screen window found` before the `raise_window` branch is ever reached (verified). The schema exposes no standalone `bring_to_front`/`launch_app` action either, and capturing such a window by explicit pid/window_id comes back `degraded` with `element_count: 0`. Only the user can move the window, so the message should say so and tell the model not to retry.

signals.title: Desktop restart reaps the live gateway but never relaunches it (WeChat/QQ go silent) — regression
signals.text: ## Summary On Windows (Hermes 0.20.0, desktop app), **every desktop-app restart force-kills the running messaging gateway and never relaunches it**. WeChat (iLink), QQ bot and Telegram go completely silent until the gateway is manually restarted. This is a regression: before this version, the old gateway survived desktop restarts (reparented), so messaging stayed online. ## Root cause In `hermes_cli/web_server.py`, when the desktop backend starts (`HERMES_DESKTOP=1`), it calls `_reap_unsupervised_gateway_orphans()` before boot, with the comment *"Before forking a fresh gateway, reap any orphan left by a previous serve session... (#77276)"*. However: 1. `_reap_unsupervised_gateway_orphans()` → `find_gateway_pids()` → `_scan_gateway_pids()` matches **any** process whose command line looks like `hermes_cli.main gateway run` (`looks_like_gateway_command_line`), including gateways started by the Windows scheduled task (`Hermes_Gateway`) or manually via `hermes gateway run`. It writes the planned-stop marker, sends SIGTERM, then SIGKILLs survivors after 5s. 2. The comment says "before **forking** a fresh gateway", but `hermes serve` does **not** spawn a gateway at all (per the same file: *"The Desktop backend is spawned as `hermes serve` — it runs neither the interactive CLI nor the messaging gateway"*). Gateway startup is delegated to external mechanisms (the login scheduled task, the update flow, or a manual `hermes gateway run`). 3. Result: **every desktop restart reaps the live gateway with no successor**. The gateway exits uncleanly (`gateway-exit-diag.log`: *"exited UNCLEANLY (no exit path ran — SIGKILL / OOM / VM death)"*), and `.gateway-planned-stop.json` is left behind. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Start the gateway (login scheduled task or `hermes gateway run`). WeChat/QQ/Telegram connect fine. 2. Close and reopen the Hermes desktop app. 3. The gateway process is gone (no exit logs; killed externally). Messages sent via WeChat/QQ get no reply until the gateway is manually restarted. Secondary symptom: the third-party skin plugin (`skin-studio`) re-asserts the configured skin on boot but only retries for ~2.5 s, while the desktop backend takes longer to become ready — so after a desktop restart the skin silently falls back to default until manually re-applied. Same class of "desktop restart breaks things that depend on the gateway/backend". ## Suggested fixes - **Option A**: when the desktop reap kills a live gateway, the desktop backend (or Electron main) should spawn a replacement immediately after reap (complete the "fork a fresh gateway" the comment promises). - **Option B**: only reap gateways that are truly unsupervised (no `gateway.pid` record / not the login scheduled-task instance), instead of every process matching `gateway run`. - **Option C**: add a config switch (e.g. `gateway.reap_on_desktop_start: false`) so users who manage the gateway externally (scheduled task / systemd / manual) can opt out. ## Workaround (user side) A 2-minute Hermes-internal cron job that checks for the gateway process and relaunches it detached with the full environment. Works, but leaves a gap and depends on the desktop backend's own cron scheduler. ## Environment - Windows 11, Hermes 0.20.0 (commit 33f8e96a72), desktop app, Python 3.12 - Platforms: WeChat (iLink), QQ Bot, Telegram (via local proxy) - `HERMES_DESKTOP=1` serve backend; gateway launched via `python.exe -m hermes_cli.main gateway run`
signals.author: zuowen7

signals.title: [Bug]: Legacy messages_fts_trigram from SQLite 3.46.1 is reported malformed by SQLite 3.53.4 during v0.18.2 → v0.20.1 upgrade
signals.text: ### Bug Description When upgrading an existing Hermes installation from v0.18.2 to v0.20.1, I found a compatibility issue with the legacy inline `messages_fts_trigram` FTS5 index. The same untouched `state.db` behaves differently depending only on the SQLite version used to open it: - SQLite 3.46.1: `PRAGMA quick_check` returns `ok` - SQLite 3.53.4: `PRAGMA quick_check` returns: `malformed inverted index for FTS5 table main.messages_fts_trigram` Importantly, normal FTS queries still work under SQLite 3.53.4. For example: `SELECT count(*) FROM messages_fts_trigram WHERE messages_fts_trigram MATCH 'test'` returned the same 3493 matches under both SQLite versions. Normal INSERT/DELETE operations on `messages`, including the legacy FTS triggers, also succeeded under SQLite 3.53.4. However, attempting to rebuild the legacy inline trigram index using: `DELETE FROM messages_fts_trigram` failed under SQLite 3.53.4 with: `sqlite3.DatabaseError: database disk image is malformed` A full reconstruction of only the trigram virtual table solved the problem: 1. Drop the three `messages_fts_trigram_*` triggers. 2. `DROP TABLE messages_fts_trigram`. 3. Recreate the same legacy inline FTS5 table with `tokenize='trigram'`. 4. Backfill it from the canonical `messages` table. 5. Recreate the triggers. After this reconstruction: - the FTS query returned exactly the same number of matches; - `PRAGMA quick_check` returned `ok`; - Hermes v0.20.1 subsequently completed its schema/config migrations successfully; - `PRAGMA quick_check` remained `ok` after v0.20.1 startup. This appears to be a compatibility edge case for a legacy inline trigram FTS index created/maintained under the older SQLite version and then opened by the newer SQLite bundled with Hermes v0.20.1. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Start with an existing Hermes v0.18.2 `state.db` containing the legacy inline `messages_fts_trigram` table. 2. Verify the untouched database using the SQLite bundled with the v0.18.2 image: - SQLite version: 3.46.1 - `PRAGMA quick_check` → `ok` - `MATCH 'test'` query → 3493 matches 3. Mount the exact same untouched `state.db` read-only into the Hermes v0.20.1 image, without running Hermes initialization or migrations. 4. Verify it using the SQLite bundled with v0.20.1: - SQLite version: 3.53.4 - `PRAGMA quick_check` → `malformed inverted index for FTS5 table main.messages_fts_trigram` - the same `MATCH 'test'` query still returns 3493 matches 5. On a separate copy of the database, perform a normal INSERT into `messages` and then DELETE it so the existing FTS triggers execute. Both operations succeed and trigram search remains functional. 6. On another copy, attempt the legacy inline rebuild pattern: `DELETE FROM messages_fts_trigram` SQLite 3.53.4 raises: `sqlite3.DatabaseError: database disk image is malformed` 7. On another clean copy, completely drop and recreate `messages_fts_trigram`, backfill it from `messages`, and recreate its triggers. 8. Verify again: - match count before rebuild: 3493 - match count after rebuild: 3493 - `PRAGMA quick_check` after rebuild: `ok` 9. Start Hermes v0.20.1 against the repaired copy. Hermes migrates the state schema to version 25 and config schema 33 → 34, and `PRAGMA quick_check` remains `ok`. ### Expected Behavior An existing valid Hermes v0.18.2 session database should remain valid when opened with the SQLite version bundled in Hermes v0.20.1. At minimum, the v0.20.1 upgrade path should detect this legacy trigram-index compatibility condition and either: - safely rebuild/recreate the affected legacy FTS index before normal runtime begins, or - clearly report that the index requires repair and provide a supported repair path. An unchanged database that passes `PRAGMA quick_check` under the previous bundled SQLite should ideally not immediately report a malformed FTS5 inverted index solely after moving to the newer bundled SQLite. ### Actual Behavior The untouched v0.18.2 database passes `PRAGMA quick_check` under SQLite 3.46.1 but immediately reports: `malformed inverted index for FTS5 table main.messages_fts_trigram` when the exact same file is opened read-only under SQLite 3.53.4. Normal trigram searches continue to work, which makes the condition easy to miss. The existing legacy rebuild approach (`DELETE FROM messages_fts_trigram` followed by reinsertion) cannot repair this state under SQLite 3.53.4 because the DELETE itself fails with: `sqlite3.DatabaseError: database disk image is malformed` Dropping and fully recreating the trigram virtual table fixes the database and preserves search results. ### Affected Component Other ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) _No response_ ### Debug Report ```shell ### Sanitized Debug Report I ran `hermes debug share --local` and reviewed the generated report before sharing anything publicly. The raw report is intentionally not attached because it contains deployment-specific identifiers unrelated to this issue. The relevant technical information is summarized below. Relevant environment: - Hermes Agent: v0.20.1 (2026.8.13) - Previous Hermes version: v0.18.2 - Python: 3.13.5 - SQLite in v0.18.2 image: 3.46.1 - SQLite in v0.20.1 image: 3.53.4 - Deployment: Docker - State database: SQLite `state.db` - Upgraded state schema: version 25 - Config migration: schema 33 → 34 Relevant database comparison using the exact same untouched `state.db`: SQLite 3.46.1: PRAGMA quick_check = ok messages_fts_trigram MATCH query = successful SQLite 3.53.4: PRAGMA quick_check = malformed inverted index for FTS5 table main.messages_fts_trigram messages_fts_trigram MATCH query = still successful and returned the same result count as SQLite 3.46.1 The database file was not modified between these two checks. Additional reproduction: - Normal INSERT into `messages` succeeded under SQLite 3.53.4. - The existing FTS insert trigger executed successfully. - Searching the trigram index after the INSERT succeeded. - DELETE of that test message also succeeded. However, attempting to rebuild the legacy inline trigram index using: DELETE FROM messages_fts_trigram failed with: sqlite3.DatabaseError: database disk image is malformed A full reconstruction of only the trigram FTS table succeeded: 1. Drop `messages_fts_trigram_*` synchronization triggers. 2. Drop `messages_fts_trigram`. 3. Recreate the legacy inline FTS5 table with `tokenize='trigram'`. 4. Backfill it from the canonical `messages` table. 5. Recreate the synchronization triggers. After reconstruction: PRAGMA quick_check = ok The trigram MATCH result count was identical before and after reconstruction. The repaired database was then started under Hermes v0.20.1. After the full Hermes startup/migration: state schema version = 25 PRAGMA quick_check = ok trigram search results remained unchanged The raw debug bundle is not attached because it contains deployment-specific information that is not required to reproduce this issue. ``` ### Operating System Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS ### Python Version 3.13.5 ### Hermes Version v0.20.1 (2026.8.13) ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ```shell Comparison using the exact same untouched database file: SQLite 3.46.1: sqlite_version= 3.46.1 quick_check= ok fts_query_ok=yes fts_test_matches= 3493 SQLite 3.53.4: sqlite_version= 3.53.4 quick_check= malformed inverted index for FTS5 table main.messages_fts_trigram fts_query_ok=yes fts_test_matches= 3493 Legacy rebuild attempt under SQLite 3.53.4: sqlite_version= 3.53.4 before_quick_check= malformed inverted index for FTS5 table main.messages_fts_trigram before_test_matches= 3493 sqlite3.DatabaseError: database disk image is malformed Full trigram drop/recreate/backfill under SQLite 3.53.4: sqlite_version= 3.53.4 before_quick_check= malformed inverted index for FTS5 table main.messages_fts_trigram before_test_matches= 3493 recreate_seconds= 30.85 after_test_matches= 3493 after_quick_check= ok Full Hermes v0.20.1 startup after repairing the copy: quick_check= ok schema_version= 25 test_matches= 3493 The production database showed the same behavior. Before reconstruction the query returned 3501 matches; after rebuilding the trigram index it still returned 3501 matches and `PRAGMA quick_check` returned `ok`. ``` ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) The evidence points to an incompatibility between the existing legacy inline `messages_fts_trigram` index representation and the newer SQLite/FTS5 implementation bundled with v0.20.1. This does not appear to be caused by the Hermes v0.20.1 schema migration itself: - the exact untouched database already produces the malformed-index result when opened read-only using SQLite 3.53.4; - the same file passes `PRAGMA quick_check` using SQLite 3.46.1; - normal FTS MATCH queries still work under both versions; - recreating only the trigram virtual table under SQLite 3.53.4 restores `PRAGMA quick_check=ok` without changing the tested search result count. The existing legacy inline rebuild implementation uses `DELETE FROM messages_fts_trigram` followed by reinsertion from `messages`. In this compatibility state, the DELETE fails before that repair can complete. A full DROP/CREATE/backfill of `messages_fts_trigram` succeeds. ### Proposed Fix (optional) Consider detecting this specific legacy FTS5 compatibility state during upgrade/startup or in `hermes sessions repair`. If the canonical `messages` table is healthy but `messages_fts_trigram` fails an FTS integrity check / SQLite quick check, the repair path for legacy inline FTS may need to fully recreate the affected virtual table rather than relying on: `DELETE FROM messages_fts_trigram` A possible recovery strategy is: 1. Detach/drop the trigram synchronization triggers. 2. Drop `messages_fts_trigram`. 3. Recreate it using the expected legacy schema. 4. Backfill from canonical `messages`. 5. Restore the current synchronization triggers. 6. Verify FTS integrity before committing the repair as successful. It may also be useful for upgrade diagnostics / `hermes sessions repair --check-only` to run an integrity check capable of detecting malformed FTS5 inverted indexes, since ordinary MATCH queries can continue to work in this state. ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

signals.title: Windows Desktop boot intermittently fails: processStartMarker powershell.exe exceeds hard 3000ms timeout before backend spawn; retry can never succeed (cached rejection)
signals.text: ## Bug Description Hermes Desktop fails to boot on Windows because `processStartMarker()` spawns `powershell.exe` with a hard 3000 ms timeout. On this machine PowerShell 5.1 cold start alone costs ~2.2–3.3 s, so the call intermittently exceeds the budget and the boot is aborted **before the backend is ever spawned**. The failing call is not about the backend at all — it queries the *Desktop's own* PID to build a start marker: ``` Command failed: powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command $p = Get-Process -Id 35132 -ErrorAction Stop; $p.StartTime.ToUniversalTime().Ticks ``` Three separate design issues compound here: 1. **Timeout too tight for PS 5.1 cold start.** `execText` hardcodes `timeout: 3000` (`apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:2957`). Measured on this host: 10 consecutive identical calls → median 2260 ms, max 3332 ms, **2/10 exceeded 3000 ms**. This makes boot a ~20% coin flip. 2. **A rejected promise is cached forever within the process.** `desktopParentStartMarker()` uses `??=` (`apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:3110-3114`). Once the first call rejects, every subsequent retry in the same Desktop process re-awaits the *same* rejected promise and fails in 0 ms. Confirmed in `desktop.log`: the first failure in a wave is +3.049 s after "Starting Hermes backend", all subsequent retries are +0 ms. The in-app Retry button therefore cannot possibly succeed. 3. **The subprocess is unnecessary for the parent's own PID.** The Linux branch of the same function reads `/proc/<pid>/stat` directly (microseconds, no subprocess). Windows spawns a whole PowerShell just to read a start time that Node already knows for itself — `Date.now() - process.uptime()*1000` resolves in 0 ms. There is no escape hatch: I grepped all 21 `process.env.HERMES_DESKTOP_*` variables in `main.ts` — none of them affect this timeout, this code path, or allow skipping the marker. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Windows 11, where PowerShell 5.1 cold start takes ≳2 s (Defender real-time protection on, no exclusions — a stock configuration). 2. Launch Hermes Desktop. 3. Boot fails ~20% of launches; when it fails, in-app **Retry** never recovers it (see cause 2 above) and the app must be fully restarted. Reproduce the timing directly, without Hermes, using the exact same call signature the Desktop uses: ```js node -e ' const {execFile}=require("child_process"); let n=0,over=0,times=[]; (function one(){ if(n++===10){times.sort((a,b)=>a-b); console.log({exceeded_3000ms:over,min:times[0],median:times[5],max:times[9]});return;} const t=Date.now(); execFile("powershell.exe",["-NoProfile","-NonInteractive","-Command", `$p = Get-Process -Id ${process.pid} -ErrorAction Stop; $p.StartTime.ToUniversalTime().Ticks`], {encoding:"utf8",windowsHide:true},()=>{const el=Date.now()-t;times.push(el);if(el>3000)over++;one();}); })()' ``` Result on this host: `{ exceeded_3000ms: 2, min: 2154, median: 2260, max: 3332 }` ## Expected Behavior Desktop boots reliably. A slow-but-successful helper query should not abort startup, and Retry should genuinely retry. ## Actual Behavior Boot aborts with `Command failed: powershell.exe ...` roughly 3.05 s after "Starting Hermes backend". The backend process is never spawned. Retry fails instantly (0 ms) because the rejected promise is cached. `desktop.log`: ``` 16:55:14.858 [boot] Starting Hermes backend for profile "default" ... 16:55:17.907 [boot] Desktop boot failed: Command failed: powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command $p = Get-Process -Id 35132 -ErrorAction Stop; $p.StartTime.ToUniversalTime().Ticks ``` (3.049 s gap = the `timeout: 3000` budget plus overhead.) ## Affected Component Desktop (Electron app) ## Operating System Windows 11 (native install, not WSL) ## Python Version 3.12 ## Hermes Version v0.20.1 (2026.8.13), commit 45af7a71f ## Root Cause Analysis `desktopParentStartMarker()` is awaited **before** `spawn()` of the backend (`main.ts:9480` and `main.ts:9802`), with no `try/catch` around it. It calls `processStartMarker(process.pid)` → `execText('powershell.exe', ...)` with `timeout: 3000`. When PowerShell 5.1 cold start exceeds 3000 ms, Node kills it and rejects. Because the caller has no fallback, the entire boot dies before the backend exists. And because `desktopParentStartMarkerPromise ??=` caches the rejected promise, no retry within that Desktop process can ever succeed. Verified this is not environment misconfiguration: - `PSModulePath` has only 3 entries; a bare session loads 0 modules — so the slowness is not a bloated user profile. - **The slowness is inherent to PowerShell 5.1 + .NET Framework JIT, not Defender.** Even with hot caches (repeated invocations), PS 5.1 still takes 1930–2872 ms — every single run lands near or above the 3000 ms budget. `pwsh` 7 on the same machine does the identical query in 791–871 ms, but `processStartMarker` hardcodes `powershell.exe` and never considers `pwsh`. - The .NET Runtime Optimization Service (`ngen queue`) is **stopped** on this machine — a common stock Windows state — which makes PS 5.1 JIT-compile its assemblies on every launch. Windows Defender real-time protection is also on (no exclusions), but removing it would NOT fix this: even hot-cached PS 5.1 calls still take ~2 s, and the subprocess is being spawned fresh each time. - Not caused by a stale PID: `backend-ownership.json` is `{"backends":[]}`. - Not `dashboard.turn_isolation` (already `false` here). - Not stacked instances: the multiple `Hermes.exe` entries are one main process plus normal Electron GPU/network/utility/audio children. - The same logic is present in the packaged `app.asar` `electron-main.mjs`, so this is not a source-vs-build mismatch. - `origin/main` still has `timeout: 3000`; updating does not fix it. Searched existing issues for `processStartMarker`, `desktopParentStartMarker`, `StartTime ToUniversalTime`, and `Command failed powershell Get-Process` — no existing report. Related but distinct: #83562 (backend self-exits 0 via parent-death watchdog), #82603 (compute host `stdin_eof`), #60144 / #68705 (15 s readiness timeout — those happen *after* the backend starts, this one happens before). ## Proposed Fix Any one of these unblocks it; ideally 1+2 together. 1. **Skip the subprocess for the parent's own PID.** Node already knows its own start time; `Date.now() - process.uptime()*1000` is exact enough for an identity marker and costs 0 ms. This mirrors what the Linux branch already achieves by reading `/proc` directly. 2. **Don't cache rejections.** Change ```js desktopParentStartMarkerPromise ??= processStartMarker(process.pid) ``` to clear the cache on failure, so Retry actually retries: ```js desktopParentStartMarkerPromise ??= processStartMarker(process.pid).catch(err => { desktopParentStartMarkerPromise = null throw err }) ``` 3. **Make the marker non-fatal.** Wrap the `await desktopParentStartMarker()` calls at `main.ts:9480` / `9802` in `try/catch` and degrade to a null marker. Losing an orphan-detection optimization is far better than refusing to boot. 4. **Raise the timeout and prefer `pwsh`.** `timeout: 3000` → 10000, and resolve `pwsh.exe` before `powershell.exe`. Note `main.ts:13204` already resolves PowerShell by absolute `System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0` path elsewhere; `processStartMarker` spawns the bare name instead — worth aligning, cf. #40927. ## Additional Logs ``` === 10x identical call, this host === {"total":10,"exceeded_3000ms":2,"min":2154,"median":2260,"max":3332} === pwsh 7 vs powershell 5.1, same query === pwsh7_ms=842 / 848 / 871 / 791 / 798 / 843 <-- 稳定 <900ms, 永不超时 ps51_ms=2872 / 2061 / 2137 / 2149 / 1930 / 2115 <-- 稳定 2-3s, 每次都在 3s 门槛附近 ^ even HOT-CACHED (repeated invocations) — slowness is PS 5.1 + .NET JIT, NOT Defender cold-scan === with Hermes' exact params (timeout:3000) === 4 of 5 calls killed at ~3.0 s === same call, timeout removed === 0 failures, ~1.96-2.83 s === .NET Runtime Optimization Service === "stopped" — PS 5.1 JIT-compiles on every launch ```

signals.title: cronjob update schema omits model/provider (drift-guard remediation is unreachable for agents)
signals.text:
## Summary The agent-facing `cronjob` tool's `update` schema omits the `model` and `provider` parameters, even though the handler accepts and applies them. As a result, when the model/provider drift guard tells the agent to pin a cron job via `cronjob action=update job_id= provider=

model=`, the agent cannot actually pass those arguments — they are not in the tool's advertised schema. ## Impact - An agent following the guard's own remediation advice cannot pin the job; the update silently applies only the other supplied fields (e.g. `name`) and reports `success: true`, leaving `model`/`provider` unset and the job still failing closed on its next run. - The remediation path is undiscoverable from the tool's self-description. ## Root cause In `tools/cronjob_tools.py`: - The **handler** applies the values (works correctly): - line 1318: `updates["model"] = _normalize_optional_job_value(model)` - line 1320: `updates["provider"] = _normalize_optional_job_value(provider)` - The **agent-facing schema** (`"parameters"` block, starting line 1463) has **no** `"model"` or `"provider"` keys — verified: `grep -c '"model"'` and `grep -c '"provider"'` over lines 1463–1619 both return `0`. ## The drift-guard message that references the broken path `cron/scheduler.py` (~line 4030) instructs: ``` Skipped to prevent unintended spend: global inference config drifted since this job was created (...), and this job is unpinned. ... To run on the new config, pin it explicitly: `cronjob action=update job_id= provider= model=` (or pin the original values to keep them). See #44585. ``` That command cannot succeed through the agent tool because `model`/`provider` are not in the schema. ## Suggested fix Add `model` and `provider` (and, for consistency, `base_url`) to the `update` action's parameters in the agent-facing schema, matching what the handler already supports. Alternatively, if the omission is intentional, the drift-guard message should not direct the agent to a parameter it cannot set. ## Reproduction 1. Have a cron job created while `model.default = anthropic/claude-opus-5` (so it snapshots that model, `model` unset). 2. Change the global model: `hermes config set model.default moonshotai/kimi-k3`. 3. `hermes config set` warns that the unpinned job will fail closed and suggests `cronjob action=update ... model=`. 4. From the agent tool, call `cronjob(action="update", job_id=..., model="moonshotai/kimi-k3", provider="openrouter")` — the arguments are rejected by schema validation / not forwarded, and the job's `model` remains `None`. ## Environment - hermes-agent @ ed5e17f - Installed via git; single Telegram gateway profile

signals.title: [Feature]: Desktop — render attached images above the user text (currently below-left, squeezing the gap to the previous reply)
signals.text: ### Problem or Use Case In Hermes Desktop, when I send a message with an image attachment, the thumbnail is rendered **below my text, on the left side** of the message. The whole user message then visually hugs the previous assistant reply — the gap between my text and the assistant's last response shrinks to almost nothing, and in long multi-turn conversations the user messages and assistant replies become genuinely hard to tell apart at a glance (they share the same width and nearly identical background). This overlaps with the readability work in #57807 / PR #71961 (bubble chat layout), but those threads cover bubble styling, not where the image sits inside the message. The composer-side image layout was already improved in #50554, but the sent-message layout is untouched. **Current behavior (Hermes Desktop)** — the orange box marks the squeezed gap between the assistant reply and my text; the image sits below-left of the text: ![hermes-current](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/linfeng961/hermes-agent/issue-img-desktop-image-position/fr-hd-image-attach-current.jpg) **For comparison (Codex Desktop)** — the image renders **above** the user text and the whole message is right-aligned, so the gap to the previous reply stays clear: ![codex-reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/linfeng961/hermes-agent/issue-img-desktop-image-position/fr-hd-image-attach-codedx.jpg) ### Proposed Solution Render attached images at the **top-right of the user message** instead of below-left: image above the text, message block right-aligned, keeping a consistent readable gap between the user message and the previous assistant reply. This should be a small, contained CSS change in the message component (image container order/alignment). If the bubble layout from PR #71961 lands, this should be folded in as the image placement rule inside a user bubble. ### Alternatives Considered - User CSS overrides — overwritten on every update, and shouldn't be needed for a default layout. - Waiting for PR #71961's bubble layout — it defines the bubble containers but not the image position within a message; this issue is the missing detail. ### Feature Type Other (Desktop UI layout) ### Scope Small (single file, < 50 lines) ### Contribution - [ ] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

signals.title: Hermes Desktop shows spurious 'boot failed' when dashboard service restarts during `hermes update`
signals.text: ## Short version Running `hermes update` from the Hermes Desktop (Windows client, remote dashboard backend) shows a scary-looking failure: ``` Desktop boot failed: Could not reach the remote Hermes gateway while refreshing its WebSocket ticket. Try reconnecting. ``` **This is a false positive.** The update and the backend restart both actually succeed; the client just runs a liveness probe during the ~10s stop/start gap of a systemd restart and treats the transient miss as fatal. It loops on "boot failed" until the new backend answers again. ## Longer version with an example Environment: Hermes v0.20.1, backend on WSL2 Ubuntu managed by systemd unit `hermes-dashboard.service` (`Restart=always`); Desktop (Win) client connected to Remote URL `http://localhost:9120`. ### What happens on a successful update 1. `hermes update` pulls new code and sees the running backend no longer matches the updated frontend. 2. It runs `systemctl restart hermes-dashboard.service`. On WSL2 the unit has `Restart=always`, so the stop/start creates a gap of roughly 10 seconds. 3. During that gap the Windows Desktop client, which holds a cached connection to the backend, issues a **liveness probe** and gets no answer. 4. The client escalates: `Cached remote Hermes backend failed liveness probe (1/3) ... (2/3) ... dropping stale connection.` then repeatedly logs `Desktop boot failed: Could not reach the remote Hermes gateway while refreshing its WebSocket ticket. Try reconnecting.` 5. A few seconds later the new backend is up and the client reconnects: `Connecting to remote Hermes backend at http://localhost:9120` -> `Remote Hermes backend is ready`. Example from the actual WSL/systemd logs during this event: ``` # sudo log: the restart that triggered the client's spurious failure 03:11:13 oleg ... COMMAND=/usr/bin/systemctl restart hermes-dashboard.service 03:11:22 systemd[1]: Stopped hermes-dashboard.service - Hermes Dashboard (Official). 03:11:22 systemd[1]: Started hermes-dashboard.service - Hermes Dashboard (Official). # desktop.log on the Windows client during the same window Cached remote Hermes backend failed liveness probe (1/3); keeping connection for retry. Cached remote Hermes backend failed liveness probe (2/3); keeping connection for retry. Cached remote Hermes backend failed liveness probe; dropping stale connection. Desktop boot failed: Could not reach the remote Hermes gateway while refreshing its WebSocket ticket. Try reconnecting. ``` The update itself finished fine: `Found 11 new commit(s) -> Code updated! -> Update complete!`, and the new backend responded normally afterwards. The only problem is the client surfacing a fake failure. ### Expected The Desktop client should tolerate a short backend downtime during a service restart - e.g. back off / keep retrying while a restart is in progress and only fail after a longer grace window - instead of declaring "boot failed" on a transient liveness miss that resolves within seconds. Thanks for looking into this. Lex by Oleg Maisak (via Hermes Agent)

signals.text: Desktop plugin load fails after update: "does not provide an export named 'McpTab'" Description After running hermes update (had to use --force-venv because the desktop app's backend process kept the venv locked), the desktop app now fails to load a desktop plugin whose module doesn't export a named McpTab, even though the plugin SDK docs only require a default-exported HermesPlugin object (id + register). Environment Hermes version: v0.20.1 (d5773bf) OS: Windows Plugin tested: [NousResearch/Hermes-Bot-Mode](https://github.com/NousResearch/Hermes-Bot-Mode) (hermes-bots), installed at %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\desktop-plugins\hermes-bots Steps to reproduce Clone https://github.com/NousResearch/Hermes-Bot-Mode into %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\desktop-plugins\hermes-bots Open Hermes desktop app → Settings → Plugins → Desktop plugins → Rescan Enable the hermes-bots plugin Plugin status shows failed with: The requested module 'blob:file:///...' does not provide an export named 'McpTab' Expected behavior Plugin loads normally (the "Bots" roster pane appears), per the [Desktop Plugin SDK docs](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/developer-guide/desktop-plugin-sdk), which state a plugin only needs a default export containing id and register. Actual behavior Plugin load fails with the error above, suggesting the desktop app now performs a hard/named import of McpTab from every desktop plugin module, regardless of whether the plugin provides one — a change not reflected in the current plugin SDK docs. Not yet confirmed whether other bundled plugins (e.g. Kanban) hit the same error when enabled — happy to test if useful.

signals.title: Background review drops gateway ephemeral session context and breaks prompt-cache prefix parity
signals.text: ## Summary The background memory/skill review fork does not inherit the parent's `ephemeral_system_prompt`. In Gateway sessions this prompt contains the pinned platform/session context, including the Feishu source and user ID block. As a result, the review request has a different system-prompt prefix from the foreground request and exact prompt-prefix caches (including llama.cpp checkpoint caches) cannot be reused. ## Evidence A captured foreground prompt contains: ```text Platform: feishu ## Current Session Context ... **Source:** Feishu ("DM with <redacted>") **User ID:** "<redacted>" ... ``` The prompt generated by the automatic background review instead contains: ```text Platform: feishu<|im_end|> ``` The first divergence is therefore the complete removal of `## Current Session Context`, not an ID rotation. The review harness message is appended afterwards. ## Source of the bug `gateway/run.py` builds the context prompt into `combined_ephemeral` and passes it as `ephemeral_system_prompt` to the foreground agent. `agent/system_prompt.py` intentionally excludes this field from `_cached_system_prompt`. `agent/background_review.py` currently copies `_cached_system_prompt` to the fork, but does not copy `ephemeral_system_prompt`: ```python review_agent._cached_system_prompt = agent._cached_system_prompt ``` Therefore the fork retains the static system prompt but loses the Gateway-injected session context. ## Impact - Feishu background reviews lose the source/user/session metadata in their effective system prompt. - The prompt prefix diverges at `Platform: feishu`, causing a full prompt-cache/checkpoint miss instead of reusing the parent's prefix. - On long contexts this can trigger expensive re-prefill and agent-side timeout/retry symptoms. - CLI sessions are not affected because they do not receive the Gateway Feishu ephemeral context. ## Proposed fix Pass the parent's ephemeral prompt when constructing the review fork, without gating it on same-model routing: ```python ephemeral_system_prompt=getattr( agent, "ephemeral_system_prompt", None ), ``` Keep the existing `_cached_system_prompt` inheritance. The effective system prompt requires both pieces, and copying the exact string preserves byte-level prefix parity without moving per-session metadata into the persisted static prompt. ## Regression test Add coverage asserting that the review fork receives an `ephemeral_system_prompt` byte-for-byte equal to the parent, with a Feishu-style `## Current Session Context` fixture. The existing cache-parity test module is a suitable location.

[Feature]: Add native support for MAIA Router (maiarouter.ai)
signals.text: ### Feature Description Add native support for [MAIA Router](https://maiarouter.ai) as an inference provider option in Hermes Agent. ### Motivation & Use Case MAIA Router is an AI model routing service that intelligently routes prompts across various LLM model endpoints, handling dynamic fallback, cost metering, and provider selection. Currently, using custom/third-party routing services requires manual base URL configuration. Having native support for MAIA Router in Hermes Agent would streamline setup for users using MAIA as their primary routing layer. Additionally, setups behind Cloudflare WAF / Zero Trust or custom proxy rules often return **404 / 403 errors** when standard SDK User-Agents are flagged or blocked. Supporting configurable `extra_headers` (e.g. `User-Agent: curl/8.7.1`) prevents Cloudflare WAF 404/403 blocks for MAIA API requests. ### API Specification & cURL Example MAIA Router uses standard OpenAI-compatible endpoints with Bearer token authentication: - **Base URL**: `https://api.maiarouter.ai/v1` - **Headers**: - `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_MAIA_API_KEY` - `User-Agent: curl/8.7.1` (Prevents Cloudflare WAF / Proxy 404/403 drops) - `Content-Type: application/json` ```bash curl https://api.maiarouter.ai/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_MAIA_API_KEY" \ -H "User-Agent: curl/8.7.1" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "maia-auto", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}] }' ``` ### Proposed Solution 1. **Provider Key & Credentials**: Support `MAIA_API_KEY` in `.env` and `maia` in provider configurations. 2. **CLI Setup & Model Picker**: Include `maia` as an option in `hermes setup` and `hermes model`. 3. **OpenAI Compatibility & Custom Headers**: Configure default base URL (`https://api.maiarouter.ai/v1`) and support `extra_headers` (e.g. `User-Agent: curl/8.7.1`) to prevent Cloudflare WAF 404/403 drops. 4. **Configuration (`config.yaml`)**: ```yaml provider: maia maia: api_key: "${MAIA_API_KEY}" base_url: "https://api.maiarouter.ai/v1" extra_headers: User-Agent: "curl/8.7.1" ``` ### Additional Context - MAIA Router Site: https://maiarouter.ai

signals.title: Trusted LAN HTTP writes remain blocked despite allowlist configuration
signals.text: ## Problem Trusted internal HTTP writes are still blocked by the terminal approval layer even when private-network access is explicitly configured as allowed. ## Environment - Hermes Agent on macOS - Active profile: default - Trusted internal HTTP service on a private LAN host - `security.allow_private_urls: true` - `security.tirith_enabled: true` - `security.tirith_fail_open: true` - `command_allowlist` includes private-LAN `curl` and `wget` patterns - `security.acked_advisories` includes the relevant Tirith private-network findings ## Reproduction 1. Have a local Markdown file, for example `/tmp/report.md`. 2. Attempt to POST it to a trusted internal HTTP service: ```bash curl --max-time 15 --data-binary @/tmp/report.md \ -H 'Content-Type: text/markdown; charset=utf-8' \ http://<trusted-lan-host>:<port>/ ``` 3. The request is blocked or times out waiting for user approval, despite the configured private-LAN allowlist and the user explicitly requesting the operation. 4. An equivalent `urllib.request` POST through `execute_code` is also blocked by the same approval boundary. ## Expected behavior For a host/port explicitly covered by `command_allowlist`, a trusted internal write should either: - execute without an approval prompt; or - produce a clear, actionable approval request in the active gateway session. The configuration should not appear to allow private-network access while the actual side-effecting operation remains blocked with no usable approval path. ## Actual behavior The tool reports that the command timed out without user response and says the user has not consented. In the Discord gateway workflow there was no visible actionable approval request to accept. The operation could not be completed. ## Impact This breaks trusted internal automation for local HTTP services, especially when an agent is operating through Discord and the user has already explicitly requested the write. It creates a confusing state where the configuration suggests private-LAN access is allowed but the side-effecting request is still unusable. ## Suggested investigation - Confirm whether `command_allowlist` is consulted before the approval prompt for commands containing private-network URLs and plain HTTP sinks. - Make the approval request visible and actionable in gateway channels, or return a stable approval identifier that can be approved through the gateway. - Distinguish trusted host/port-specific LAN patterns from arbitrary private-network writes. - Add an integration test covering a POST to a trusted internal HTTP service with a matching allowlist entry. - Clarify the precedence between Tirith findings, `tirith_fail_open`, `command_allowlist`, `security.allow_private_urls`, and gateway approval mode.

signals.title: ACP mode: interrupting a turn with a hung tool call crashes adapter with 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'startswith'
signals.text: ## Bug: ACP mode — interrupting a turn with a hung tool call crashes the adapter with `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'startswith'` (JSON-RPC -32603) ### Environment - Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (2026.8.13), Windows 11 - ACP mode (`hermes acp`), driven by an ACP host (Paseo daemon v0.4.0) - Provider: deepseek ### Scenario (observed) 1. Agent starts a turn that runs a terminal tool call which hangs (here: `ls`/`find` under git-bash/MSYS on Windows — known MSYS hang when traversing directories). 2. While the turn is stuck waiting on the tool result, follow-up messages from the user are queued (`Queued for the next turn (N queued)`) and cannot interrupt. 3. The user interrupts the hung tool (SIGINT; the bash subprocess exits with code 130). 4. Instead of recovering cleanly, the ACP turn dies with a JSON-RPC internal error, observed on the host side at the moment of interruption: ``` error: "Internal error: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'startswith'" code: -32603 data: {"details": "'NoneType' object has no attribute 'startswith'"} ``` The message format (`'NoneType' object has no attribute 'startswith'`) is a Python `AttributeError`, so the crash is inside the Hermes ACP adapter, not the host. ### Impact - The interrupted turn fails instead of resuming/recovering. - Queued follow-up messages are dropped/blocked by the failed turn state and need a manual interrupt of the whole turn to get the agent back. ### Logging gap (why exact line is unknown) `acp_adapter/entry.py` (`_setup_logging`) routes all adapter logging **only to stderr**, and the host does not persist the child's stderr, so no traceback is available. Only the JSON-RPC error message reached the host. Likely spots (`.startswith()` on possibly-`None` values in `acp_adapter/server.py`): - line 506: `data if data.startswith("data:")` — `data` may be `None` - lines 1667 / 1690 / 1712: `user_text.startswith(...)` — `user_text` may be `None` - line 2012: `final_response.startswith(...)` — `final_response` may be `None` on an interrupted/empty turn (most likely, since this fires on interruption) ### Requests - Guard `.startswith()` calls against `None` in the interrupt/busy paths (fix the crash). - Log tracebacks for adapter-internal errors (so the exact site is diagnosable). - Ensure queued messages are flushed or explicitly failed when a turn dies, instead of leaving the session stuck.

signals.title: Classic CLI: Shift+letter prints literal [27;2;<code>~ instead of capital on Ghostty (modifyOtherKeys level 2)
signals.text: ## Summary In the classic interactive CLI, pressing **Shift + letter** (e.g. `Shift+W`) prints the literal text `[27;2;87~` into the prompt buffer instead of the capital letter `W`. Same for every Shift+letter/digit/punct combo: `Shift+H` -> `[27;2;72~`, `Shift+C` -> `[27;2;67~`, etc. Root cause: the CLI requests xterm **modifyOtherKeys level 2** (`CSI >4;2m`) from allowlisted terminals, which makes the terminal report *every* modified key as a `CSI 27;mod;code~` escape sequence. prompt_toolkit (and Hermes' `pt_input_extras.py`) only decode the Enter/Backspace variants of those sequences; the Shift+letter sequences fall through the VT100 parser and are inserted as literal characters. ## Environment - Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (2026.8.13), git install - Python 3.13.12 (conda), prompt_toolkit 3.0.52 - macOS 26.5.2 (Tahoe), Apple Silicon - Terminal: Ghostty, `TERM=xterm-ghostty`, `TERM_PROGRAM=ghostty` ## Steps to reproduce 1. Start the classic CLI: `hermes` in a Ghostty window. 2. Type `Shift+W`. ## Expected vs actual - Expected: `W` is inserted. - Actual: `[27;2;87~` is inserted (the `ESC` byte is consumed by the parser as the Escape key; the rest lands in the buffer as literal text). ## Root cause `cli.py`: - `_EXTENDED_ENTER_KEYS_SEQ = "\x1b[>4;2m"` (level 2) is written to the terminal when `_terminal_supports_extended_enter_keys()` matches the allowlist (`TERM_PROGRAM in {iTerm.app, WezTerm, ghostty, vscode}`, `xterm-ghostty`, kitty, tmux, `WT_SESSION`). - Level 2 semantics: **all** modified keys are reported as `CSI 27;mod;code~`, where `code` is the ASCII value of the resulting (shifted) character. `Shift+W` -> `\x1b[27;2;87~`. - Stock prompt_toolkit 3.0.52 `ANSI_SEQUENCES` only maps the Enter variants: `\x1b[27;2;13~`, `\x1b[27;5;13~`, `\x1b[27;6;13~`. - `hermes_cli/pt_input_extras.py` additionally maps Shift/Ctrl+Enter and Cmd+Backspace / Cmd+ForwardDelete (`\x1b[27;9;127~`, `\x1b[3;9~`, ...). - No mapping exists for `\x1b[27;2;<65..126>~` (Shift+letters/digits/punct), so `Vt100Parser` splits the sequence into `Escape` + `[27;2;87~` literal characters. The feature's stated intent is "report Shift+Enter distinctly" — every sequence Hermes actually decodes has an unmodified form that is a **control character** (Enter=13, Backspace=127). Level 2 buys nothing over level 1 for this use case and breaks all Shift+letters. ## Evidence Minimal parser repro (prompt_toolkit 3.0.52, before any aliases installed): ```python from prompt_toolkit.input.vt100_parser import Vt100Parser events = [] p = Vt100Parser(events.append) p.feed('\x1b[27;2;87~') print([(e.key, e.data) for e in events]) # [(<Keys.Escape: 'escape'>, '\x1b'), ('[', '['), ('2', '2'), ('7', '7'), # (';', ';'), ('2', '2'), (';', ';'), ('8', '8'), ('7', '7'), ('~', '~')] ``` ## Proposed fix `cli.py`: request **level 1** instead of level 2: ```diff -_EXTENDED_ENTER_KEYS_SEQ = "\x1b[>4;2m" +_EXTENDED_ENTER_KEYS_SEQ = "\x1b[>4;1m" ``` Level 1 still reports modified keys whose unmodified form is a control character — `Shift+Enter` (`27;2;13~`), `Ctrl+Enter` (`27;5;13~`), `Cmd+Backspace` (`27;9;127~`) — exactly the set `pt_input_extras.py` decodes — while Shift+letters arrive as plain capitals again. All existing aliases keep working; nothing Hermes maps requires level 2. ## Verification - `python -m pytest tests/cli/test_cli_shift_enter_newline.py tests/cli/test_cli_cmd_backspace.py tests/cli/test_cli_terminal_shortcuts.py tests/cli/test_ctrl_enter_newline.py` -> 30 passed, 2 skipped. - Manual: after restart, `Shift+letter` inserts the capital; `Shift+Enter` still inserts a newline. ## Scope Affects every terminal in the allowlist (`iTerm.app`, WezTerm, ghostty, vscode, kitty, tmux), not just Ghostty — any of them will emit unmapped `CSI 27;...~` sequences under level 2. The fix is a one-line constant change; the whole bug class (unmapped modified-key sequences leaking as literal text) is resolved for Shift+keys.

signals.title: fix(mcp): WSL2 child PID tracking + MCP subprocess resilience (salvage #10250)
signals.text: ## Summary Combines two fixes and their bugfixes into one coherent PR. ### 1. WSL2 child PID tracking (ps --ppid) On WSL2, /proc/<pid>/task/<pid>/children returns empty for multi-threaded processes (Hermes has 12+ threads), causing _snapshot_child_pids() to always return an empty set. MCP server subprocess PIDs are never tracked, so they accumulate as orphans across reconnects. **Fix:** try `ps --ppid` first (works on WSL2, macOS, Linux), fall back to /proc/children, then psutil. ### 2. MCP subprocess resilience (salvaged from #10250, sege66) Three stacked fixes for long-running gateway stability. **a) Survive subprocess drops and reset retry counter** - MCPServerTask.run() previously counted reconnect attempts over the server's entire lifetime. Now the consecutive-retry counter is reset when the previous session was healthy (>= 30s uptime). - Polls tracked subprocess PIDs every 5s via _any_pid_alive. - Unexpected clean exit from transport is treated as disconnect, not a break from the reconnect loop. **b) Close stale-server recovery gaps** - register_mcp_servers / discover_mcp_tools now treat session=None / task.done() as stale and reclaimable instead of leaving dead entries permanently blocking re-registration. **c) Make recovery invisible to the agent** - Two-attempt loop in tool handlers: on first ClosedResourceError, schedules reclaim, waits up to 15s for fresh subprocess, retries the same call. Agent only sees a slightly slower call, never an error. ### 3. Bug fixes from the PR #10250 merge The salvage merge introduced several runtime errors that are fixed here: - Duplicate ClientSession in _run_stdio finally block referencing already-closed streams. - _rpc_lock, _reclaim_inflight, _pending_refresh_tasks declared in __slots__ but never initialized in __init__. - _pending_refresh_tasks typed as list but used with set methods. - _connected_at missing from stdio initialization path. ## Test plan - [x] Hermes gateway starts and connects Telegram - [x] All 3 MCP servers (searxng, pgvector-memory, ssh-manager) connect - [x] MCP tool calls succeed (ssh_execute to moreno, niqepsilon) - [x] Keepalive fires without triggering reconnect storms - [x] No orphan MCP subprocesses accumulate over multiple reconnect cycles - [x] pytest tests/tools/test_mcp_tool.py passes (inherits 173 existing tests + 8 regression tests from #10250) - [x] Tested on WSL2 (Ubuntu, kernel 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2)

signals.title: fix(computer_use): use get_window_state for CUA vision capture (#39242)
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? Fixes `computer_use(capture, mode="vision")` when using the cua-driver backend. cua-driver 0.5.x does not expose a standalone `screenshot` MCP tool. The previous Hermes vision capture path called that missing tool, which caused vision captures to silently return an empty `CaptureResult(width=0, height=0, png_bytes=0)`. SOM capture had a related issue: it called `get_window_state` without `capture_mode="som"`, so it could return an AX tree without the screenshot payload. Width/height metadata was also never read from cua-driver's `structuredContent`. This PR: - routes vision, SOM, and AX captures through `get_window_state` - passes `capture_mode="vision"` for vision capture - passes `capture_mode="som"` for SOM capture - extracts `screenshot_width` / `screenshot_height` from `structuredContent` when present - preserves AX no-image behavior ## Related Issue Fixes #39242. ## Verification Regression tests were added in `tests/tools/test_cua_backend_capture.py` covering all issue layers: - vision mode calls `get_window_state`, not `screenshot` - vision mode passes `capture_mode="vision"` - vision mode returns the screenshot image - SOM mode passes `capture_mode="som"` - SOM mode returns screenshot + parsed elements - vision/SOM dimensions are populated from `structuredContent` - missing `structuredContent` remains safe and leaves dimensions at `0x0` - AX mode remains no-PNG Fail-without-fix proof on upstream/main: 6 failed, 3 passed. Final focused validation after rebase: ```text /Users/evinova-self/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python3 -m pytest tests/tools/test_computer_use.py tests/tools/test_cua_backend_capture.py -v -o "addopts=" --tb=short 83 passed, 1 warning ``` ## Competitor / duplicate check No open PR references #39242 directly. Keyword search found #38664 with partial topic overlap around computer_use capture dimensions, but it does not fix the non-existent `screenshot` tool call or missing `capture_mode` handling, so it is not a blocking duplicate. Auto-published by Moonsong via Path B automated pipeline.

signals.title: feat(memory): core/extended tiering with [core] prefix and search action
signals.text: ## Summary Add memory tiering to reduce system prompt token cost. Entries prefixed with `[core]` are always injected into the system prompt. Entries without the prefix are extended — available on-demand via the new `search` action. ## Problem Memory entries accumulate over time and all get injected into the system prompt on every turn. This causes prompt pollution (#22563) and wastes tokens in the cached prefix — the single most expensive part of every API call. The current mitigation is a flat `memory_char_limit` that truncates everything equally, with no way to distinguish always-needed facts from situational ones. ## Solution - **`[core]` prefix**: marks entries for always-injection. Case-insensitive (`[CORE]` and `[Core]` also recognized). Stripped in the snapshot. - **Backward compatible**: when no entries have `[core]`, all entries go in — existing users see zero change. - **`search` action**: case-insensitive substring match against all entries (core + extended). The on-demand retrieval path for extended memory. - **User profile unaffected**: always all-in (small and always relevant). - **Snapshot header**: when tiering is active, the header shows `(core tier — N extended entries available via search)` so the model knows extended entries exist. ## Dogfood results 45 entries → 27 core + 18 extended. System prompt memory block drops from 9,439 to 5,342 chars (43% reduction). Combined with `protect_last_n=6`, per-turn token floor drops ~1,024 tokens. ## Changes | File | What | |------|------| | `tools/memory_tool.py` | `[core]` prefix filtering in `_render_block`, `search` action on `MemoryStore`, schema update, blocked-entry prefix preservation | | `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py` | Extract shared `_execute_memory_tool()` — both dispatch paths now call one function (prevents parameter drift) | | `agent/tool_executor.py` | Use shared `_execute_memory_tool()` instead of inline closure | | `tests/tools/test_memory_tiering.py` | 20 tests: prefix recognition, case-insensitivity, snapshot filtering, header signaling, blocked-core guard, search action, schema | | `tests/tools/test_memory_tool.py` | 1 test: blocked core entry pass-through | ## Related issues - Closes the structural gap behind #22563 (memory pollution) - Related to #32198 (tiered injection — different axis, model-specific char limits) - Serves the same goal as #35575 (prompt cache efficiency) ## Test plan - [x] 111 memory-related tests pass, no regressions - [x] 20 new tiering-specific tests - [x] Dogfooded on live instance — `memory(action="search")` working, tiering active
